context: In each of the examples given below, a pair of triangles is shown. Equal parts of triangles in each pair are marked with the same signs. Observe the figures and state the test by which the triangles in each pair are congruent.
stem: In the first pair of figure 3.19, \(\triangle ABC\) and \(\triangle PQR\) are drawn. Side AB and side PQ each carry one tick, side BC and side QR each carry two ticks, and side AC and side PR each carry three ticks. Complete : By ......... test, \(\triangle ABC \cong \triangle PQR\).
diagramNote: Fig. 3.19 (i) — two triangles ABC and PQR, with all three pairs of corresponding sides marked equal (one, two and three ticks respectively).

context: In each of the examples given below, a pair of triangles is shown. Equal parts of triangles in each pair are marked with the same signs. Observe the figures and state the test by which the triangles in each pair are congruent.
stem: In the second pair of figure 3.19, \(\triangle XYZ\) and \(\triangle LMN\) are drawn. Side XY and side LM each carry one tick, \(\angle Y\) and \(\angle M\) each carry the same arc mark, and side YZ and side MN each carry two ticks. Complete : By ......... test, \(\triangle XYZ \cong \triangle LMN\).
diagramNote: Fig. 3.19 (ii) — triangles XYZ and LMN, with XY = LM (one tick), the included angles at Y and M marked equal, and YZ = MN (two ticks).

context: In each of the examples given below, a pair of triangles is shown. Equal parts of triangles in each pair are marked with the same signs. Observe the figures and state the test by which the triangles in each pair are congruent.
stem: In the third pair of figure 3.19, \(\triangle PRQ\) and \(\triangle STU\) are drawn. \(\angle P\) and \(\angle S\) each carry the same mark, side PR and side ST each carry two ticks, and \(\angle R\) and \(\angle T\) each carry the same mark. Complete : By ......... test, \(\triangle PRQ \cong \triangle STU\).
diagramNote: Fig. 3.19 (iii) — triangles PQR and STU, with the angles at P and S marked equal, side PR = side ST (two ticks), and the angles at R and T marked equal.

context: In each of the examples given below, a pair of triangles is shown. Equal parts of triangles in each pair are marked with the same signs. Observe the figures and state the test by which the triangles in each pair are congruent.
stem: In the fourth pair of figure 3.19, \(\triangle LMN\) and \(\triangle PTR\) are drawn. \(\angle M\) and \(\angle T\) are each marked as right angles, side LM and side PT each carry one tick, and side LN and side PR — the sides opposite the right angles — each carry two ticks. Complete : By ......... test, \(\triangle LMN \cong \triangle PTR\).
diagramNote: Fig. 3.19 (iv) — two right-angled triangles, right angle at M and at T, with LM = PT (one tick) and the hypotenuses LN = PR (two ticks).

context: Observe the information shown in pairs of triangles given below. State the test by which the two triangles are congruent. Write the remaining congruent parts of the triangles.
stem: From the information shown in figure 3.20, in \(\triangle ABC\) and \(\triangle PQR\) : \(\angle ABC \cong \angle PQR\); seg BC \(\cong\) seg QR; \(\angle ACB \cong \angle PRQ\). Complete the following : \(\therefore \triangle ABC \cong \triangle PQR\) ....... ......... test. \(\therefore \angle BAC \cong\) ......... (corresponding angles of congruent triangles). seg AB \(\cong\) ......... and ......... \(\cong\) seg PR (corresponding sides of congruent triangles).
diagramNote: Fig. 3.20 — triangles ABC and PQR side by side; the angles at B and Q carry the same mark, the angles at C and R carry the same mark, and sides BC and QR each carry two ticks.

context: Observe the information shown in pairs of triangles given below. State the test by which the two triangles are congruent. Write the remaining congruent parts of the triangles.
stem: From the information shown in figure 3.21, in which seg PS and seg QR intersect at the point T, in \(\triangle PTQ\) and \(\triangle STR\) : seg PT \(\cong\) seg ST; \(\angle PTQ \cong \angle STR\) .... vertically opposite angles; seg TQ \(\cong\) seg TR. Complete the following : \(\therefore \triangle PTQ \cong \triangle STR\) ....... ......... test. \(\therefore \angle TPQ \cong\) ......... and ......... \(\cong \angle TRS\) (corresponding angles of congruent triangles). seg PQ \(\cong\) ......... (corresponding sides of congruent triangles).
diagramNote: Fig. 3.21 — seg PS and seg QR cross at T; PT and TS each carry two ticks, QT and TR each carry one tick.
_note: The book prints 'shown in the figure,,' with a doubled comma; transcribed here with a single comma.

stem: From the information shown in figure 3.22, state the test assuring the congruence of \(\triangle ABC\) and \(\triangle PQR\). Write the remaining congruent parts of the triangles. In the figure, \(\angle A\) and \(\angle Q\) are each marked as right angles, side AB and side PQ each carry one tick, and side BC and side PR — the sides opposite those right angles — each carry two ticks.
diagramNote: Fig. 3.22 — two right-angled triangles: in the first the right angle is at A with C below A and B to the right; in the second the right angle is at Q with R below Q and P to the left. AB = PQ (one tick) and the hypotenuses CB = PR (two ticks).

stem: As shown in the following figure 3.23, in \(\triangle LMN\) and \(\triangle PNM\), \(LM = PN\) and \(LN = PM\). Write the test which assures the congruence of the two triangles. Write their remaining congruent parts.
diagramNote: Fig. 3.23 — L is the upper-left vertex and P the upper-right, with M and N on a common lower base; seg LN and seg PM cross each other. LM and PN each carry one tick, LN and PM each carry two ticks, and seg MN is common to both triangles.

stem: In figure 3.24, seg AB \(\cong\) seg CB and seg AD \(\cong\) seg CD. Prove that \(\triangle ABD \cong \triangle CBD\).
diagramNote: Fig. 3.24 — a kite ABCD with B at the top, D at the bottom, A at the left and C at the right, and the diagonal seg BD drawn. Sides AB and CB each carry two ticks; sides AD and CD each carry one tick.

stem: In figure 3.25, \(\angle P \cong \angle R\) and seg PQ \(\cong\) seg RQ. Prove that \(\triangle PQT \cong \triangle RQS\).
diagramNote: Fig. 3.25 — \(\triangle PQR\) with Q at the top, P at the lower left and R at the lower right; S is a point on side PQ and T is a point on side QR. Seg PT and seg RS are drawn and cross inside the triangle. No parts are tick-marked; the given facts are stated in words.
